tagline: Bay Area Government Corruption Podcast Series
description: Investigative true-crime podcast revealing California Bay Area scandals where powerful individuals escaped justice through legal maneuvering, connections, and systemic failures
region: California Bay Area (San Jose, San Francisco, Silicon Valley, surrounding counties)
targetAudience: Listeners interested in government accountability, legal system analysis, and Bay Area corruption

episodes.title: The Union Boss Who Smuggled Opioids: Joanne Segovia's Zero-Jail Deal
Stealing from Housing: Clarke Howatt's $3.9M Embezzlement
The Building Inspector's Decade of Bribes: Rodolfo Pada
Half a Year for $20K Bribes: Ken Wong's Minimal Sentence
A $36K Rolex and a Construction Deal: Florence Kong's Corruption

commonThemes: Legal system failures allowing wealthy/connected individuals to escape consequences
Restitution used as a replacement for prison time
Public service records cited to minimize sentences for federal crimes
Bay Area's systemic corruption across government agencies
The two-tiered justice system revealed through sentencing disparities
investigativeAngles: Why addiction narratives reduce sentences for drug smuggling
How restitution can replace prison time for embezzlement
What makes a 14-year bribery scheme worth only 13 months
Why parole officers get half-year sentences for federal bribery
The Rolex and the contract: Tracking contractor corruption
producerNotes: Each episode focuses on the 'escape mechanism' - the legal, procedural, or systemic factor that allowed justice to be subverted. Emphasize the public impact of these corruptions and contrast with typical sentencing for ordinary citizens.
